title: Jack Carey's daughter, a guitarist and a paralyzed trumpeter
summary: They try to recall names of a guitarist and a trumpeter who suffered a stroke.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Did you ever locate Evelyn Carey?
Yeah, she come to the hospital one day. Oh, yeah. So, she sure did. You know where she's at? She gave me her address. Nah, I got it somewhere at home at the house.
Oh, we'll have to find that, man. That's Jack's daughter, I mean.
Well, I can find out easy. Yeah, good. I know where to find out.
You told me one time about a guitarist being Poison. You don't remember his name, do you?

No, I can't think of that boy's name now, but he was a nice looking, brown-skinned kid. Lot of girls around him all the time. And he was a good, good guitar player too, but I don't know what his name is now.
What about this trumpet player that got paralyzed, you remember? One time you told me, Poison, about this woman told a man that if he hit her, he'd never use that arm anymore. Oh, yeah, that was.
I've forgotten his name too, but I knew he got a paralyzed stroke.
Where did he live, that guy, you know him? That well?
He was in, I think he's from Mississippi. Oh, yeah.
Yeah. He wasn't a New Orleans guy then? No, no.
